# Milestone brief — verification-contract-spike-1

**Title:** Windows isolation route bake-off: Job Object+restricted token vs container/WSL2
**Kind:** spike
**Roadmap:** verification-contract (plans/verification-contract/roadmap.yaml)
**Status:** planned
**Lane:** next
**Target:** 2026-08-11 -> 2026-08-13

## Parent epic

- verification-contract-e2 — Windows isolation boundary
  Spike Job Object + restricted token against container/WSL2 on the attack suite's resource cases, record the choice as an ADR with measured overhead, and land the boundary itself (no network, read-only toolchain/env, writable per-call scratch only, CPU/memory/process/file-size caps, kill-and-teardown on violation) so untrusted Lean stops running unconfined on Windows. Enabler: unblocks verification-contract-e3, which executes untrusted candidates inside it.

## Summary

(none in roadmap — derive scope from the acceptance criteria)

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given the attack suite's resource cases (heartbeat/memory/fork bombs, filesystem/network escape attempts), when both Job Object+restricted token and container/WSL2 routes are measured within the 3-day timebox, then pass/fail and overhead are recorded per route in an ADR
2. Given neither route meets the isolation bar within the timebox, when the spike concludes, then Lean stays disabled-by-default and R5 targets are checked via the documented manual operator fallback instead of m2 proceeding
